text: Testing plays a vital role in software development. Unit tests check small pieces of code, like individual functions, to ensure they work correctly on their own. Integration tests, on the other hand, verify that different parts of a system work together smoothly, catching problems that unit tests might miss. A popular approach called test-driven development asks developers to write tests before the actual code, which helps clarify requirements and prevents bugs early on. Together, these practices build confidence. When tests pass regularly, developers feel safer making changes, knowing that any breakage will be detected quickly. This reduces stress and leads to more reliable software.
